findings.detail: The dev lane previously used `cancel-in-progress: false` with the note that a running run always completes. The head sets `cancel-in-progress: true` on group `release-dev-branch-dev`. The called release-provider.yml runs inside this caller's concurrency scope, so a second `workflow_dispatch` on `dev` cancels the whole in-flight run, including Developer ID signing, notarization, R2 staging and registration. Registration or staging can then be left half-finished, and each new run gets a new run_number version. Any repository writer can dispatch (no inputs, `github.ref == refs/heads/dev` is the only check) and can keep cancelling releases, or leave staged but unregistered artifacts. This replaces the push trigger, which only ledger-bypass accounts could fire. Fix: keep `cancel-in-progress: false` for the `dev` group, or cancel only before the signing and publish jobs. Restrict dispatch to authorized actors.
findings.title: Dev-branch signing/publish run can now be cancelled mid-flight by a later dispatch
